plainLanguage: Beaumont uses the 2021 International Residential Code and energy code and the 2020 National Electrical Code. It is in Jefferson County, inside the state windstorm area: Beaumont is in TDI's Inland II zone (110 mph old-basis, about 143 mph in today's terms), so your house needs wind-resistant design and an engineer's windstorm certificate to get TWIA insurance. The city itself requires an engineer windstorm certification for any building of 120 sq ft or more. Since April 2026 the state certifies windstorm work to the 2024 code, so your engineer may use slightly different wind numbers. Much of Beaumont is in mapped flood zones; if yours is, the floor must sit above the flood level (we assume 1 ft above until confirmed). The building permit is about $0.50 per sq ft plus $150 plan review, roughly $1,600 for a 2,400 sq ft home with garage. No impact fees were found. The city cannot require brick.
